There is no evidence of obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or remote code execution triggered at parse time.

All variable definitions follow typical AUR packaging patterns and do not deviate into malicious behavior during sourcing. Issues such as skipped checksums or unpinned sources are noted for later audit but do not affect the safety of running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

Since the file is well-known and from an official source, and no execution occurs from it directly, this does not constitute a supply-chain risk.

No evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, obfuscation, or unauthorized system modifications is present. All operations align with standard AUR packaging workflows for Python packages that depend on external protobuf definitions and prebuilt tools.
